## Arithmetic partial sums {#ss4-formulas .ar-lesson .ar-formulas-slide}

$$S_n=\sum\limits_{k=1}^{n}a_k$$

::: {.split .ar-formula-columns}
::: {.column-block}
<h3>First and last terms known</h3>

$$S_n=\frac{n}{2}(a+a_n)$$

:::
::: {.column-block}
<h3>First term and difference known</h3>

$$S_n=\frac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d]$$

:::

:::

<p class="ar-mean-interpretation">Number of terms × average of the first and last terms.</p>

<div class="ar-reference"><h3>HSC formula sheet · Sequences and series</h3><div class="ar-reference-crop"><img src="../media/hsc-reference-sheet-sequences.png" alt="The arithmetic partial-sum line from the HSC reference sheet: S n equals n over two times 2a plus n minus one times d, or n over two times a plus a n."></div></div>

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 20 · Complete the partial-sum result</p>

::: notes

Here a is the first term and a_n=l is the last term included in S_n. The number of terms is n when the sum starts at index 1. Choose either form according to the information supplied. Do not use the last index as the count when a sum starts later.
